status: Stage-specific plan to be hashed before fitting; post-development exploratory, not prospective preregistration
question: How do common-reference CES-D8 item contrasts between hearing-screen groups change when continuous age and sex enter the latent distribution and then the non-anchor response functions?
scope: A bounded four-model M2/probit marginal-likelihood pilot with numerical and local-fit diagnostics. No Bayesian shrinkage, forests, anchor selection or new causal analysis in this stage.

data.inclusion: Reuse frozen final complete-case domain; do not exclude records on the basis of new model results
covariates: age10 = (released age capped at 90 - 70)/10; original -7 explicitly represents 90+
female = 1 for released indsex 2, 0 for indsex 1
data.missingness_rule: Stop if age or sex is invalid in the frozen domain; no silent extra exclusion or imputation
data.overlap: Report age-by-sex overlap across hearing groups descriptively; retain original domain and flag sparse cells, no data-driven trimming

measurement.structure: M2 correlated affective/somatic factors; affective i1,i4,i5,i6,i7 and somatic i2,i3,i8
measurement.binary_link: probit, P(Yj=1 | theta,x) = Phi(bj + x*Dj + exp(logaj + x*Ej)*theta_factor)
measurement.anchor_set: AS01: i1,i4,i2,i3, retained transparently as the prior post hoc reference, not empirically validated
measurement.anchor_constraints: All direct intercept and log-loading covariate effects on these four anchors are zero for hearing, age and sex. Age/sex invariance is a NEW stronger assumption in this stage.
measurement.factor_location_scale: Mean = X beta, SD = exp(X gamma) separately for each factor; reference O0, age70, male has means0 and SDs1
measurement.factor_correlation: rho = tanh(r0+rH*hearing01); no age/sex moderation of correlation

estimation.criterion: Mean negative weighted marginal log likelihood, with within-hearing-group weights normalized to the group sample size
estimation.estimator_change: Old main analyses used DWLS. Compare new covariate models against the new hearing-only marginal-likelihood baseline, not directly attribute changes from old DWLS to covariate adjustment.
estimation.optimizer: Bounded L-BFGS-B, analytic gradients, deterministic initialization and one fixed perturbed start; report all attempts
estimation.quadrature: Independent 2D Gauss-Hermite-normal integration. Fit at21 nodes per dimension and check31. If that numeric check fails, refit at31 and check41; if needed refit41 and check61. No further adaptive changes.
estimation.boundary_rule: Any parameter within1e-5 of numerical bounds, nonpositive observed information direction, unresolved multistart disagreement or quadrature failure is flagged; do not treat optimization status alone as valid estimation
estimation.numerical_audit: Independent finite differences, response-pattern probabilities sum to1, stage embedding, weighting scale invariance, synthetic local rank, mandatory observed-Hessian diagnostics at the higher check order using central differences of analytic gradients. Missing Hessian checks mean not numerically certified.
estimation.reference_integration_check: Compare the closed-form common-reference probabilities with independent adaptive one-dimensional integration over [-10,10] at all observed age/sex profiles and both hearing groups; tolerance1e-4. Fixed-parameter closed-form probabilities are not compared across GH orders. Save target changes between different-order refits if refinement occurs.
estimation.initialization: First stage uses generic engine initialization; later stages embed the preceding model with new coefficients zero. The second start adds 0.08*sin(1..p) to each coefficient, clipped to0.001 inside fixed bounds. Each quadrature refinement starts from the preceding selected solution and the same fixed perturbation.
estimation.hessian_step: Central gradient differences: step=1e-4*max(1,abs(parameter)); symmetric Hessian eigenvalues and condition number reported. Positive definite means minimum eigenvalue>1e-7. No standard errors from this matrix.

estimands.primary_display: For each non-anchor item and each model, O1-minus-O0 endorsement probability averaged over the same fixed standard-normal latent coordinate and over the pooled empirical age/sex distribution using the declared normalized weights
estimands.formula: At each age/sex: Phi((b+x1D)/sqrt(1+exp(2*(loga+x1E)))) - Phi((b+x0D)/sqrt(1+exp(2*(loga+x0E)))); then take the same age/sex reference-weighted average
estimands.not_used_in_reference: Fitted hearing-group-specific latent means and variances are not integrated into the reference contrast
estimands.profile_display: Age60,70,80 separately for male/female, with underlying sample support counts; these are descriptive model profiles, not subgroup hypothesis tests
estimands.interpretation: Model- and anchor-conditional response contrasts. Not observed prevalence, corrected CES-D scores, clinical diagnosis, hearing effects or treatment effects

diagnostics.selection: No preferred model chosen by p values, desirable signs, or improvement in a single residual
diagnostics.local_fit: Within hearing groups, compare survey-weighted observed item endorsement probabilities and all28 pair joint endorsement probabilities with model-implied averages at the observed covariates. Highlight i2/i7 but retain all pairs.
diagnostics.metric_warning: Binary joint-probability residuals here are different from old DWLS tetrachoric correlation-moment residuals; do not directly compare their numerical sizes
diagnostics.inference: No p values, confidence intervals, causal claims or confirmed-DIF declarations in this first marginal-likelihood implementation. Household/GOR identifiers remain available in RAM for future design-variance work; weights alone do not provide cluster-robust uncertainty.

history: Both prior partitions and the pooled sample were already examined. New age/sex models are exploratory. All original analyses and the current manuscript remain unchanged.
outputs: all model attempts and numerical diagnostics
reference contrasts and age/sex profiles when numerically admissible
privacy: Participant data stay in local RAM. No participant rows, original IDs, individual latent scores or fitted respondent-level objects are written or transmitted. Only aggregate results and model parameters are saved.
failure_policy: Preserve failed fits and diagnostics. Do not simplify the primary structure, replace anchors, add parameters or change the sample after seeing results. Technical implementation corrections require a logged amendment; no silent retries.

references.title: A more general model for testing measurement invariance and differential item functioning
references.role: MNLFA framework; this implementation is a bounded custom extension, not a verbatim software reproduction

references.title: Bayesian penalty methods for evaluating measurement invariance in moderated nonlinear factor analysis
references.role: Possible later extension, not executed here
